62026-a-yankee-girl-at-antietam.title: Antietam
62026-a-yankee-girl-at-antietam.creator: Alice Turner Curtis
62026-a-yankee-girl-at-antietam.description: A book by Alice Turner Curtis. When Roxy reached the wall she climbed to its top and stood looking anxiously along the gray road that skirted a wooded hill, and in a few moments a brown horse, harnessed to a light wagon, and driven by a bareheaded girl whose red hair gleamed in the June sunshine, trotted into sight and came rapidly down the hill.

arxiv-2107-00016.title: Primordial Black Hole Evaporation and Dark Matter Production: II. Interplay with the Freeze-In/Out Mechanism Preprint: FERMILAB-PUB-21-305-T, NUHEP-TH/21-07, CP3-21-42, IPPP/21/01
arxiv-2107-00016.creator: Andrew Cheek a, Lucien Heurtier b, Yuber F. Perez-Gonzalez c,d,e, Jessica Turner b
arxiv-2107-00016.description: Abstract We study how the evaporation of primordial black holes (PBHs) can affect the production of dark matter (DM) particles through thermal processes. We consider fermionic DM interacting with Standard Model particles via a spin-1 mediator in the context of a Freeze-Out or Freeze-In mechanism.

arxiv-2204-11528.title: Multiple orthogonal polynomials, d d -orthogonal polynomials, production matrices, and branched continued fractions
arxiv-2204-11528.creator: Alan D. Sokal
arxiv-2204-11528.description: Abstract I analyze an unexpected connection between multiple orthogonal polynomials, d d -orthogonal polynomials, production matrices and branched continued fractions. This work can be viewed as a partial extension of Viennot’s combinatorial theory of orthogonal polynomials to the case where the production matrix is lower-Hessenberg but is not necessarily tridiagonal.

arxiv-2206-14910.title: Isoperimetric Formulas for Hyperbolic Animals
arxiv-2206-14910.creator: Érika Roldán, Rosemberg Toala-Enriquez
arxiv-2206-14910.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Érika Roldán, Rosemberg Toala-Enriquez. An animal is a planar shape formed by attaching congruent regular polygons along their edges. In 1976, Harary and Harborth gave closed isoperimetric formulas for Euclidean animals. Here, we provide analogous formulas for hyperbolic animals. We do this by proving a connection between Sturmian words and the parameters of a discrete analogue of balls in the graph determined by hyperbolic tessellations. This reveals a complexity in hyperbolic animals that is not present in Euclidean animals.

arxiv-2208-01802.title: Mutual Information Scoring: Increasing Interpretability in Categorical Clustering Tasks with Applications to Child Welfare Data
arxiv-2208-01802.creator: Pranav Sankhe, Seventy F. Hall, Melanie Sage, Maria Y. Rodriguez, Varun Chandola, Kenneth Joseph
arxiv-2208-01802.description: Abstract Youth in the American foster care system are significantly more likely than their peers to face a number of negative life outcomes, from homelessness to incarceration. Administrative data on these youth have the potential to provide insights that can help identify ways to improve their path towards a better life.

arxiv-2407-18863.title: Sigma-compactness of Morse boundaries in Morse local-to-global groups and applications to stationary measures
arxiv-2407-18863.creator: Vivian He, Davide Spriano, Stefanie Zbinden
arxiv-2407-18863.description: Abstract . We show that the Morse boundary of a Morse local-to-global group is σ \sigma -compact. Moreover, we show that the converse holds for small cancellation groups. As an application, we show that the Morse boundary of a non-hyperbolic, Morse local-to-global group that has contraction does not admit a non-trivial stationary measure.

arxiv-2409-16258.title: SWARM: Replicating Shared Disaggregated-Memory Data in No Time
arxiv-2409-16258.creator: Antoine Murat, Clément Burgelin, Athanasios Xygkis, Igor Zablotchi, Marcos K. Aguilera, Rachid Guerraoui
arxiv-2409-16258.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Antoine Murat, Clément Burgelin, Athanasios Xygkis, Igor Zablotchi, Marcos K. Aguilera, Rachid Guerraoui. Memory disaggregation is an emerging data center architecture that improves resource utilization and scalability. Replication is key to ensure the fault tolerance of applications, but replicating shared data in disaggregated memory is hard.

arxiv-2410-08013.title: Probing nonlinear spin dynamics in canted easy-plane antiferromagnets using spin-rectification effects
arxiv-2410-08013.creator: A. El Kanj, S. Mantion, I. Boventer, P. Bortolotti, V. Cros, A. Anane, O. Gomonay, R. Lebrun
arxiv-2410-08013.description: Abstract We investigate spin-rectification phenomena in canted antiferromagnets, closely connected to the family of altermagnetic materials. Our results show that excitation efficiency is significantly enhanced by the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction. Antiferromagnetic dynamics can be detected through spin-Hall magnetoresistance and bolometric effects, with an efficiency reaching up to mV/W.

arxiv-2410-23036.title: Evidence for a Sharp CO Snowline Transition in a Protoplanetary Disk and Implications for Millimeter-wave Observations of CO Isotopologues Facilities: ALMA
arxiv-2410-23036.creator: Chunhua Qi, David J. Wilner
arxiv-2410-23036.description: Abstract Observations of CO isotopologue emission from protoplanetary disks at millimeter wavelengths are a powerful tool for probing the CO snowline, an important marker for disk chemistry, and also for estimating total disk gas mass, a key quantity for planet formation.

arxiv-2501-12581.title: Approximate Puzzlepiece Compositing
arxiv-2501-12581.creator: Xuan Huang, Will Usher and Valerio Pascucci
arxiv-2501-12581.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xuan Huang, Will Usher and Valerio Pascucci. The increasing demand for larger and higher fidelity simulations has made Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR) and unstructured mesh techniques essential to focus compute effort and memory cost on just the areas of interest in the simulation domain. The distribution of these meshes over the compute nodes is often determined by balancing compute, memory, and network costs, leading to distributions with jagged nonconvex boundaries that fit together much like puzzle pieces.

arxiv-2511-15745.title: Structured Extraction of Vulnerabilities in OpenVAS and Tenable WAS Reports Using LLMs
arxiv-2511-15745.creator: Beatriz Machado 1 , Douglas Lautert 1 , Cristhian Kapelinski 1 , Diego Kreutz 1
arxiv-2511-15745.description: Abstract This paper proposes an automated LLM-based method to extract and structure vulnerabilities from OpenVAS and Tenable WAS scanner reports, converting unstructured data into a standardized format for risk management. In an evaluation using a report with 34 vulnerabilities, GPT-4.1 and DeepSeek achieved the highest similarity to the baseline (ROUGE-L greater than 0.7).

arxiv-2512-06140.title: RationalFunctionApproximation.jl: Rational Approximation On Discrete and Continuous Domains
arxiv-2512-06140.creator: Tobin A. Driscoll
arxiv-2512-06140.description: Abstract Unlike polynomials, rational functions can represent functions having poles or branch cuts with root-exponential convergence and no Runge phenomenon. Recent developments of the AAA and greedy Thiele algorithms have sparked renewed interest in computational rational approximation. The RationalFunctionApproximation package supplies the fastest known implementations of these methods and the only arbitrary-precision ones.

pmc-12542075.title: NR2F6 regulates Temozolomide resistance in glioma via the E2F2-PARP1 pathway
pmc-12542075.creator: Bo Wang, Pengfei Xue, Rongrong Li, Yaxin Liang, Zhaohao Wang, Lili Yan, Qianqian Zhang, Conghui Tian, Lili Yi, Cuncun Yang, Xin Li, Juan Zheng
pmc-12542075.description: BackgroundGlioma is the most common primary malignant brain tumor in adults. Temozolomide (TMZ) represents a standard-of-care chemotherapeutic agent in glioblastoma (GBM). However, the development of drug resistance constitutes a significant hurdle in the treatment of malignant glioma. Elucidating the mechanisms of temozolomide (TMZ) resistance in glioma is of critical clinical importance for improving patient prognosis and developing novel therapeutic strategies.

pmc-12585892.title: The hidden biodiversity knowledge split in biological collections
pmc-12585892.creator: Gabriel Nakamura, Bruno Henrique Mioto Stabile, Livia Estéfane Fernandes Frateles, Matheus Lima Araujo, Emanuel Bruno Neuhaus, Manoela Maria Ferreira Marinho, Melina de Souza Leite, Aline Richter, Liuyong Ding, Tiago Magalhães da Silva Freitas, Bruno Soares, Weferson Júnio da Graça, Mario R. Moura,
pmc-12585892.description: Ecological and evolutionary processes generate biodiversity, yet how biodiversity data are organized and shared globally can shape our understanding of these processes. We show that name-bearing type specimens—the primary reference for species identity—of all freshwater and brackish fish species are predominantly housed in Global North museums, disconnected from their countries of origin.

pmc-12652952.title: Outdoor Natural Versus Built Experiments: A Scoping Review and Methodological Recommendations for Psychological Science
pmc-12652952.creator: Shahar Almog, Maribel Rodriguez Perez, Meredith S. Berry
pmc-12652952.description: The beneficial effects of exposure to nature on health and well-being, including enhanced relaxation and improved mood and attention, are well-established. Less evidence exists on understudied outcomes related to clinical populations (e.g., substance use outcomes, decision-making), mainly from laboratory experiments warranting outdoor studies.

pmc-12802003.title: Towards “Zero by 30”, the Kenyan case: a systematic exploration of barriers to rabies policy implementation through systems thinking
pmc-12802003.creator: Laurent Smets, Sanjeet Kumar Jaiswar, Valentijn Stienen, Benedict Mueke Muma, Vincent Okungu, Nico Vandaele, Catherine Decouttere
pmc-12802003.description: IntroductionRabies is a neglected tropical disease (NTD) that disproportionately affects marginalized communities, despite the availability of effective vaccines. In response, the “Zero by 30” global strategic plan aims to eliminate dog-mediated human rabies deaths by 2030. However, localized barriers such as underreporting, fragmented vaccine supply and insufficient governance often impede progress, particularly for settings in Kenya.

pmc-13197832.title: Affordable Arsenic Detection Device Using Handmade Lokta Paper for Decentralized and Sustainable Manufacturing
pmc-13197832.creator: Ramdeep Shrestha, Bhanu Bhakta Neupane, Basant Giri
pmc-13197832.description: The reliance on centralized manufacturing systems often shows vulnerability of global supply chains, as evidenced by disruptions during the COVID‐19 pandemic and geopolitical conflicts. This study reports an affordable and portable paper strip sensor for arsenic detection in groundwater, developed using distributed manufacturing and sustainability principles.

uslaw-usc-t36-s170313.title: 36 U.S.C. § 170313 — Annual report
uslaw-usc-t36-s170313.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t36-s170313.description: United States Code, Title 36 (Patriotic And National Observances, Ceremonies, And Organizations); Part B (Organizations); Chapter 1703 (Pearl Harbor Survivors Association). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The corporation shall submit an annual report to Congress on the activities of the corporation during the prior fiscal year. The report shall be submitted at the same time as the report of the audit required.
